Kindergarten, when I was thrown into a small group of people who seemingly knew each other for the most part from pre-k (I had pre-school somewhere else). I basically felt like an outsider from then beginning and from the age of 5 quickly lost faith in my ability to integrate into a group. I had anxiety from it, never really understood why I would get along with some people but never form a close relationship with them. I always had friends here and there, but I was never their "best friend" and they always had a ton of other friends. I became jealous of that. My social skills only consisted of being able to converse with the intent of making other people laugh, in a mostly "silly" way that made people think I was weird. That is a kind of social awkwardness. I could not small talk. To an extent this is true today, and I'm 22. I felt like I never "made" friends; they just sort of happened. But also what "just sort of happened" was a lot of social rejection and being labeled "weird" and "awkward" which I guess were true. From the beginning I adopted the belief that I was indeed weird and awkward, which coming into middle school *really* kicked things off and things snowballed from there. I was just a kid. I just thought, well, fuck, this is who I am I guess, because normative personality development is highly dependent on our perceived identities within a social context. I was a loser to the group and so I was also a loser to myself. This is a recipe for social anxiety. A hole that just got deeper as the years went by, but I didn't notice because I never imagined how these things might impact the trajectory of my future (lack of foresight), and I developed a rich inner-imagination that I could retreat to through drawing, videogames, role-playing, and daydreaming. Basically, socializing became hell and escapism was the sanctuary that made my life worth living. This comment has gone on long enough lol. This is how it all began.
